headline: Paraguay takes over Ueno Bank, with 3 million customers, and freezes its deposits
body:
Paraguay’s Central Bank on Tuesday took over Ueno Bank, one of the country’s largest banks, after its solvency ratio fell below 50% of the legal minimum, and froze all its assets and liabilities, including the savings of some 3 million customers and more than US$800 million in public funds. The bank immediately suspended all its services.
“We proceeded to close the entity; therefore, neither the app, nor the cards, nor any service of the entity is active from today,” said Liana Caballero, a member of the Central Bank’s board, which took the decision unanimously. According to its own figures, Ueno’s customers are equivalent to 60% of the country’s adult population, and it manages public funds including about US$380 million from the Social Security Institute, which runs pensions and public healthcare.
The Deposit Guarantee Fund covers savings of up to 75 minimum wages, about 228 million guaraníes or roughly US$38,200 per person. Those with larger balances will have to wait for the Superintendency of Banks’ final accounting. “The priority will always be small savers,” said Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo, who described the situation as “an isolated, one-off event” and said the financial system “remains sound and healthy”.
According to Carvallo, the takeover followed months of investigation that revealed loans to companies linked to the bank’s owners. On October 18, the Association of Banks of Paraguay had asked the Central Bank to report on the solvency of institutions that benefited from facilities in merger processes and warned about a bank’s credit exposure, which it did not identify, to companies in its own group. Days earlier, senators from the ruling party and the opposition had called on President Santiago Peña to dismiss the Central Bank’s leadership , which Peña backed.
Carvallo, who ran Ueno Bank before Peña appointed him to head the Central Bank in 2023, said he had signed his resignation, although he will remain in office until the bank’s resolution is complete. According to the Paraguayan press, several of the bank’s executives were detained, including its president, Miguel Vázquez.
The crisis had immediate political fallout. Vice President Pedro Alliana “paused” his bid for the ruling Colorado Party’s presidential nomination in order to “put the house in order”. The opposition Authentic Radical Liberal Party said it would push for impeachment proceedings against Peña and Alliana. “They plundered the pensioners’ money and this cannot be left like this,” said its presidential hopeful Ricardo Estigarribia, according to the newspaper ABC Color. In 2024, the Social Security Institute’s purchase of about US$32 million in Ueno bonds caused controversy; Peña, who called the reports a “media campaign”, was a shareholder in Ueno Holding, not the bank, and sold those shares in April 2025.

headline: Markets react to the US midterms: the dollar falls and gold rises
body:
The US dollar weakened against major currencies on Wednesday morning and gold rose more than 2% to above US$4,000 an ounce as markets assessed the Democratic victory in the midterm elections, which will give the opposition control of both chambers of Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.
The dollar index, which measures its value against a basket of currencies, remained in negative territory near 101.50, and the yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note fell below 4.95%, according to financial analysis platform FXStreet. Wall Street index futures were mixed. The dollar’s biggest fall was against the Swiss franc, at 0.4%. The euro briefly rose above US$1.1250, its highest in two weeks, before easing to 1.1230, and sterling extended its winning streak to a sixth day above US$1.3450, ahead of an expected Bank of England rate rise on Thursday.
Analysts at Germany’s Commerzbank warned that “US equities, and in particular the tech-heavy Nasdaq, are likely to come under pressure today”, and that because the dollar’s recent strength had benefited from equity-related capital inflows, “dollar weakness could consolidate somewhat further in the coming hours”. In the longer term, they said a more constructive political debate in the United States, “admittedly a very remote possibility”, could reduce the political risk premium priced into the dollar.
Trump told The Wall Street Journal that the Iran war was “partially to blame” for the Republican defeat and that he has no plans for personnel changes in his administration.

headline: Chinese chipmaker Hua Hong bets big on silicon photonics amid AI boom
body: China’s second-largest contract chipmaker, Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor, is aggressively expanding into silicon photonics, as the company looks to capture the next wave of the global artificial intelligence infrastructure boom. Speaking on an earnings call with analysts on Thursday, Hua Hong chairman and president Bai Peng said the company planned to significantly expand its footprint in silicon photonics – a critical technology used in AI optical modules – during its next major capacity expansion in 2027. “We want to participate in all silicon-based devices [inside optical modules],” Bai said, adding the sector is one of the two areas – along with power management chips – in which it wants to add “significantly more capacity”.
